proof_summary: Lucas’s theorem modulo \(3\) and parity of central binomial coefficients give \(A_n\equiv(-1)^n\pmod 3\) and \(A_n\equiv1\pmod4\); subtracting suitable multiples of the first Hankel column then extracts factors \(3^n\) and \(4^n\), with the initial determinant supplying \(16\mid a(n)\) also in the remaining case. In the binomial expansion of \((1+u)^{1/8}\), the \(3^m\)-divisibility cancels the degree-\(m\) scaling denominator, while \(16^d\)-divisibility cancels the \(2\)-adic denominators of \(\binom{1/8}{d}\); all odd-prime denominators are absent, so every coefficient is integral and the binomial identity gives the required eighth power.
